questionText:
Consider the IEEE-754 single precision floating point numbers $P = \text{0xC1800000}$ and $Q = \text{0x3F5C2EF4}$.

Which one of the following corresponds to the product of these numbers (i.e., $P \times Q$), represented in the IEEE-754 single precision format?
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze number $P = \text{0xC1800000}$
Converting $P$ to binary representation:
$P = \text{1 10000011 00000000000000000000000}_2$
• Sign bit ($S_P$) = $1$ (Negative)
• Biased Exponent ($E_P$) = $10000011_2 = 131_{10}$
• Actual Exponent ($e_P$) = $131 - 127 = 4$
• Mantissa ($M_P$) = $0$
So, $P = -1.0 \times 2^4 = -16$.

Step 2: Analyze number $Q = \text{0x3F5C2EF4}$
Converting $Q$ to binary representation:
$Q = \text{0 01111110 10111000010111011110100}_2$
• Sign bit ($S_Q$) = $0$ (Positive)
• Biased Exponent ($E_Q$) = $01111110_2 = 126_{10}$
• Actual Exponent ($e_Q$) = $126 - 127 = -1$
• Mantissa ($M_Q$) = $10111000010111011110100_2$

Step 3: Compute the product $P \times Q$
• Resulting Sign bit ($S$) = $S_P \oplus S_Q = 1 \oplus 0 = 1$ (Negative)
• Multiplying $Q$ by $-2^4$ shifts the exponent of $Q$ by $+4$ without changing its fraction/mantissa bits.
• New Actual Exponent ($e$) = $e_Q + 4 = -1 + 4 = 3$
• New Biased Exponent ($E$) = $3 + 127 = 130_{10} = 10000010_2$
• Mantissa ($M$) remains identical to $M_Q = 10111000010111011110100_2$

Step 4: Reconstruct 32-bit floating-point result
• Binary: $\text{1 10000010 10111000010111011110100}_2$
• Grouping into 4-bit nibbles: `1100 0001 0101 1100 0010 1110 1111 0100`
• Hexadecimal: `0xC15C2EF4`

Hence, the correct option is C.
